result_expr: Derivative(phi(x, y, t), t) + M*(2*W*phi(x, y, t)*(1 - phi(x, y, t))*(1 - 2*phi(x, y, t)) - kappa*(Derivative(phi(x, y, t), (x, 2)) + Derivative(phi(x, y, t), (y, 2))))

steps.statement: F = ∫_Ω [kappa/2 (phi_x^2 + phi_y^2) + W phi^2 (1-phi)^2] dA; each integrand term is in J m^-3
steps.operation: restate the given functional and check units

steps.statement: δF = d/dε F[phi+ε η]|_{ε=0} = ∫_Ω [kappa (phi_x η_x + phi_y η_y) + f'(phi) η] dA, where f = W phi^2 (1-phi)^2
f'(phi) = 2W phi (1-phi)^2 - 2W phi^2 (1-phi) = 2W phi (1-phi)(1-2 phi), in J m^-3
∫_Ω kappa ∇phi·∇η dA = ∮_∂Ω kappa η ∇phi·n ds - ∫_Ω kappa η (phi_xx + phi_yy) dA
δF = ∫_Ω [2W phi (1-phi)(1-2phi) - kappa (phi_xx + phi_yy)] η dA
steps.operation: drop the boundary term because η = 0 on ∂Ω, then substitute S3 and S4

steps.statement: mu = δF/δphi = 2W phi (1-phi)(1-2phi) - kappa (phi_xx + phi_yy), in J m^-3
steps.operation: identify mu from δF = ∫ mu η dA for every admissible η

steps.statement: phi_t = -M mu; M mu has units m^3 J^-1 s^-1 · J m^-3 = s^-1, matching phi_t
steps.operation: state the Allen-Cahn law and check units

steps.statement: R = phi_t + M [2W phi (1-phi)(1-2phi) - kappa (phi_xx + phi_yy)] = 0
steps.operation: add M mu to both sides and substitute S6

assumptions_used: kappa, W and M are constant and positive (so kappa comes out of the derivatives in S4)
phi is smooth on the closure of Omega (needed for the integration by parts in S4)
the variation of phi vanishes on the boundary of Omega (removes the boundary term in S5)
